newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank says net profit grew 4.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank says net profit grew 4.8 percent.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, said Tuesday its net income rose by 4.8 percent last year, with operating profits soaring 37 percent
The net profit of 2.2 billion marks ($1.3 billion), however, lagged earnings growth at Deutsche's major domestic rivals, although it was at the high end of analysts' forecasts.
The operating profit of 5.8 billion marks ($3.4 billion) was above expectations.
Analysts had expected net profit would be stagnant or show only minor growth due to a series of blows to Deutsche's earnings last year.
The bank was hit by the estimated 200 million pound ($323 million) cost of compensating investors for alleged mismanagement at three unit trusts run by London-based Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.
But analysts expected little direct impact on earnings because Deutsche was expected to have used reserves to foot the bill.
The MGAM affair, which came to light last September, was only the latest in a string of problems.
The bank is estimated to have added more than 200 million marks ($117 million) to risk provisions to cover a bail-out of engineering group Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG.

Also, two major shareholdings, Daimler-Benz AG and construction group Philipp Holzmann, omitted dividends for 1995, costing Deutsche 219 million marks ($128.6 million) in lost income, according to analysts' estimates.
